mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as the low rate environment reduces discount rates for equity cash flows and increases risk appetite. The relationship is continuous: lower FEDFUNDS values correlate with higher returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 250 and with a monthly growth rate exceeding 2% signals inflationary pressure that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as the Fed may tighten policy to combat inflation.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 250 and monthly change > 0.02, or the rank correlation between the trigger condition and returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is stable (change < 0.01) and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising rapidly (monthly change > 0.02), it indicates the Fed is not responding to inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to heightened uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS change < 0.01 and CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.02
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when the trigger condition is met, or the rank correlation between the interaction signal and returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts (HOUST > 850) signal a late-cycle economy with potential overheating, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the Fed may tighten policy to cool the market.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when HOUST > 850, or the rank correlation between HOUST and returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5%, it signals a tight labor market that may lead to inflationary pressures and Fed tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE < 5, or the rank correlation between UNRATE and 5-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is stable (change < 0.01), it indicates a labor market tight without corresponding monetary policy response, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to rising inflation expectations.
regime_hint: non-responsive monetary policy to labor market tightness
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when the trigger condition is met, or the rank correlation between the interaction signal and returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of industrial production (INDPRO) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as strong industrial activity reflects robust economic growth that supports corporate earnings and risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO is above 90, or the rank correlation between INDPRO and 5-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When residential fixed investment (RSAFS) falls below 400,000 million dollars, it signals a slowdown in the housing market that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as the housing sector is a key component of the economy and its weakness may indicate broader economic concerns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS < 400000, or the rank correlation between RSAFS and 60-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.
